ISSUE36_DEVELOPMENT_REVISION.SCOPE: One unversioned /conversations resource tree; BFE Drive Internal Auth over UDS with session-bound DPoP; current Chat authorization and membership visibility intervals; direct/group conversations; PostgreSQL message/history/read state and durable wakeToken mapping; ntfy v2.34.0, ntfy Android distributor v1.25.2 and UnifiedPush connector 3.3.5; Android system notification and protected token resolution.

CONSTRAINTS.CONSTRAINT: No /v1 or /v2 conversation APIs and no new WebSocket transport.
Every protected Chat request validates session-bound DPoP and independently checks current Chat authorization.

The realtime wake payload allowlist is exact: protocol version and opaque wakeToken only. It excludes message text, conversation/account identifiers, document IDs/titles and document content. Document metadata is available only through authorized history.
wakeToken is a reusable, non-authorizing conversation reference without arbitrary fixed TTL.
No independently switchable Chat enabled/disabled application state exists. Protected operations use the standard DPoP, current-authorization, validation, and dependency-health contracts.
ntfy plus UnifiedPush is the sole active realtime transport. Runtime interoperability remains unverified and is a mandatory gate.
The required -ntfy-origin is independent of -public-origin; each complete Endpoint must match its HTTPS origin and the pinned ntfy Android Endpoint format.

Outbound ntfy requests use -ntfy-timeout defaulting to 5s, propagate cancellation and reject redirects. Each claim has a unique AttemptID and a WorkerID unique to the running backend worker process instance; WorkerID is never reused after restart. The ten-second lease is renewed every three seconds only before permit grant. Only expired ATTEMPTED rows without a permit are automatically changed to terminal UNKNOWN; DISPATCHING is not recovered by lease expiry. Outcome writes are fenced by delivery, attempt, worker and permit identity. No automatic retry.

The existing backend worker process may initiate HTTP only after AuthorizeDeliveryDispatch atomically grants a unique one-time dispatch_permit_id and transitions ATTEMPTED to DISPATCHING while the ten-second lease is unexpired. The permit remains valid after lease expiry and is bound to WorkerID, which uniquely identifies the running worker process instance and is not reused after restart. No separate Dispatcher, child process or process manager is introduced. Lease expiry alone never recovers DISPATCHING; a trusted existing process-lifecycle source must confirm that exact worker process has terminated before recovery to UNKNOWN. If confirmation is unavailable, leave DISPATCHING unchanged indefinitely. No automatic retries.

Service reachability is controlled by process/service availability and infrastructure controls, not an application-level Chat switch. No database/admin-service availability provider or Device-based identity is introduced.
Target a fresh database; no legacy-data migration, compatibility layer or legacy-client support.

A background worker in the existing backend claims committed outbox intents after message commit. Each claim stores a unique attempt_id, WorkerID identifying the unique running process instance, and a lease expiry ten seconds from database time; the worker renews every three seconds. HTTP runs outside transactions with a five-second timeout. Recovery atomically marks only expired ATTEMPTED rows without a permit UNKNOWN; conditional attempt/worker checks fence stale workers. DISPATCHING is never recovered by timer. No automatic re-dispatch.

The client receives push through the approved UnifiedPush connector/distributor pair.

ROUTE.AUTHORIZATION: Validate the current DPoP-bound session, resolve the durable token mapping, then recheck current account membership and message visibility before returning conversationId. Token possession is not authorization.
ROUTE.FAILURE_MAPPING: Malformed JSON, missing wakeToken field, wrong field type or other request-schema violations map to VALIDATION_ERROR/400. Invalid authentication maps to AUTH_INVALID/401; unavailable Internal Auth maps to AUTH_UNAVAILABLE/503. A syntactically valid request containing a malformed, stale, unknown, revoked or otherwise unauthorized token value maps to NOT_FOUND/404 with no conversation identity or protected data disclosed.

Current eligibility is rechecked before any publication; an ineligible recipient is terminally skipped without HTTP.
A conclusive failure before dispatch authorization is terminal and is not retried.
The permit-owning worker process records a conclusive HTTP failure using the matching permit and WorkerID.
The ten-second lease expires before dispatch authorization; atomic recovery wins only if no permit has moved the row to DISPATCHING.

Deferred transition only; it is not enabled in the current architecture. No trusted process-lifecycle source or recovery operation is defined, so no current operation may perform this transition. DISPATCHING remains unchanged indefinitely after worker disappearance. A future separately approved architecture revision must define the trusted evidence source and recovery contract before this transition can be enabled. Lease expiry, elapsed time, missing heartbeat, database connectivity and service restart are not proof of process termination.
The permit-owning worker process records timeout, cancellation or transport ambiguity for the single HTTP request; the outcome is terminal and is never retried.
The permit-owning worker process records ntfy acceptance for the matching one-time permit; this does not prove the recipient has history access.

STATE_MODEL.STATE: No prior committed result exists for this idempotency key and authenticated sender scope.
A valid first request has atomically stored its message and idempotency result.
A repeated request with identical content returns the original result and creates no duplicate logical message or notification.
A repeated request with different content returns 409 Conflict and creates no new message or notification.
STATE_MODEL.TRANSITION: A new valid request commits message and idempotency result atomically.
A subsequent request with identical content returns the original result without another logical notification.
A subsequent request with different content is rejected with 409 Conflict and no additional side effect.

STATE_MODEL.STATE: No subscription record exists for this account and Endpoint.
A validated UnifiedPush endpoint and encryption material are stored as protected subscription data.
The destination is no longer eligible for future delivery attempts.
STATE_MODEL.TRANSITION: Registration succeeds only after DPoP and endpoint-origin checks; storage failures do not create a partial subscription.
A validated replacement updates the protected destination data.
Authorized removal disables future delivery attempts to this destination.

TRANSACTION.ATOMIC_WORK: Validate current sender membership; serialize message ordering against concurrent membership mutations; allocate conversation-scoped order; persist message and idempotency result; establish eligible-recipient ordering and persist one durable delivery-outbox intent per eligible account-owned subscription. Identical idempotent replay creates no new outbox intent.
TRANSACTION.COMMIT_POINT: PostgreSQL commit makes the message, idempotency result and delivery-outbox intents durable together. A failed commit produces no push publication. The HTTP request path may return after this commit without waiting for outbound delivery.
TRANSACTION.AFTER_COMMIT: A background worker claims each committed recipient intent, rechecks current recipient eligibility, ensures the wakeToken mapping is durable, then performs outbound ntfy HTTP outside all database transactions and records a terminal outcome without secrets.
TRANSACTION.FORBIDDEN: Do not perform network I/O inside a database transaction. Do not treat ntfy as part of PostgreSQL atomic commit. Do not roll back committed message state because publication fails. Do not automatically retry a delivery attempt in the first implementation.

TRANSACTION.ATOMIC_WORK: Acquire the conversation-scoped lock; verify the conversation is a group; verify active membership and the caller's current owner/admin role; update the group name.
TRANSACTION.COMMIT_POINT: Commit only after the kind, membership and role checks and the name update all succeed. Any failure rolls back the transaction without changing the name.
TRANSACTION.FORBIDDEN: Do not perform kind, membership or role checks outside this transaction as the authorization basis for the write; do not change membership, roles or visibility intervals.

TRANSACTION.ATOMIC_WORK: Acquire the same conversation-scoped lock used by DP36-TX-MESSAGE; verify direct kind and the viewer's active membership; upsert only that viewer's hidden state.
TRANSACTION.COMMIT_POINT: Commit the hidden-state change only after all checks and the upsert succeed. Failure rolls back the whole operation.
TRANSACTION.SERIALIZATION: Incoming-message auto-unhide in DP36-TX-MESSAGE and HideDirect share the same conversation lock. The final hidden state follows the serialized operation order.
TRANSACTION.FORBIDDEN: Do not check kind or membership in separate unprotected operations; do not change peer visibility, messages or membership.

TRANSACTION.ATOMIC_WORK: Claim only QUEUED intents. In one short transaction set ATTEMPTED, create unique attempt_id, store WorkerID identifying the unique running backend worker process instance (never reused after restart), and set lease_expires_at to database time plus 10 seconds. Renew every 3 seconds only while the matching ATTEMPTED attempt has an unexpired lease; each renewal extends expiry by 10 seconds. Before HTTP, AuthorizeDeliveryDispatch atomically checks delivery_id, attempt_id, WorkerID, ATTEMPTED status and unexpired lease; it creates a unique dispatch_permit_id bound to the same WorkerID, changes the state to DISPATCHING and commits. The permit authorizes one HTTP attempt by that worker process and remains valid after the original lease expires. Record the outcome in a separate short transaction only when delivery, attempt, WorkerID, permit and DISPATCHING state all match. No database transaction spans HTTP.
TRANSACTION.COMMIT_POINT: RecoverExpiredDeliveryLeasesUnknown atomically changes only expired ATTEMPTED rows without a permit to terminal UNKNOWN. Authorization and lease recovery serialize on the same row: whichever commits first determines whether a permit exists; if recovery wins, authorization fails, and if authorization wins, lease recovery cannot change DISPATCHING. The current architecture defines no trusted process-lifecycle source and no recovery operation for DISPATCHING. Therefore, DISPATCHING remains unchanged indefinitely after worker disappearance; do not infer termination from lease expiry, elapsed time, missing heartbeat, database connectivity or service restart. Any future DISPATCHING recovery requires a separately approved architecture revision defining the trusted evidence source and recovery contract. Concurrent recovery cannot transition the same row twice. UNKNOWN means delivery may or may not have occurred.
TRANSACTION.FORBIDDEN: No automatic retries or transition from UNKNOWN back to QUEUED, ATTEMPTED or DISPATCHING. Do not issue HTTP without a committed permit, issue more than one HTTP request for a permit, let a lease timeout revoke an already-issued permit, recover DISPATCHING solely because its lease expired, allow stale result writes, hold a transaction across HTTP, or delay the message response. HTTP timeout is 5 seconds; lease duration 10 seconds; renewal interval 3 seconds.

TRANSACTION.ATOMIC_WORK: Serialize membership/role mutation, close or open the correct bounded visibility interval, and persist authorization state consistently with message eligibility ordering.
TRANSACTION.COMMIT_POINT: After the membership change commits, every subsequent protected request evaluates the new state; historical visibility gaps remain closed.

TRANSACTION.ATOMIC_WORK: Persist the opaque token-to-conversation mapping before any event carrying the token is published; resolve through a read path that rechecks authorization on each request.
TRANSACTION.COMMIT_POINT: Mapping persistence does not authorize the caller. Resolution has no token-consumption side effect.

TRANSACTION.ATOMIC_WORK: Advance only the authenticated account's marker monotonically for the specified conversation.
TRANSACTION.FORBIDDEN: Never change another account's marker or advance a marker based on untrusted client-supplied account identity.

TRANSACTION.ATOMIC_WORK: For create, persist a new subscription record owned by the authenticated AccountID and return its opaque subscriptionId. For replace/delete, resolve the record using both authenticated AccountID and subscriptionId and mutate only that record. Each account may own an unbounded number of records; subscriptionId is not a device identifier or authorization capability.
TRANSACTION.FORBIDDEN: Invalid Endpoint input is not persisted or used for an outbound request. Cross-account record access must not disclose record ownership or secrets. Do not log Endpoint capabilities or encryption secrets.

FAILURE_PATH.TRIGGER: Message commit succeeds but ntfy publication fails, times out, or an executor stops during delivery.
FAILURE_PATH.PATH: Keep the committed message, idempotency result and durable per-subscription outbox intent; record a sanitized terminal outcome without tokens, Endpoint capability URLs or payload secrets; do not roll back. Timeout, cancellation or transport ambiguity for the one authorized HTTP request becomes terminal UNKNOWN. Lease expiry triggers automatic UNKNOWN only for ATTEMPTED with no committed permit. After permit grant, never recover DISPATCHING by timer. If the worker process terminates without a result, wait for trusted confirmation from an existing process-lifecycle source; if unavailable, leave DISPATCHING unchanged indefinitely. Do not requeue or retry. UNKNOWN does not prove delivery failed; clients recover through authenticated history.
FAILURE_PATH.ACCESS_CHECKS: History recovery independently checks current session, Chat state, membership and message visibility.
FAILURE_PATH.SIDE_EFFECTS: Only delivery outcome is recorded; no duplicate message is created.
FAILURE_PATH.END_STATE: Message remains committed and available to currently authorized viewers through history.

FAILURE_PATH.TRIGGER: An idempotency key is repeated after a prior request.
FAILURE_PATH.PATH: Compare replay with original result under the defined sender/key scope. Identical content returns original result; different content returns 409 Conflict.
FAILURE_PATH.ACCESS_CHECKS: Authenticate and authorize the current request before returning protected results.
FAILURE_PATH.SIDE_EFFECTS: No new logical message or notification for identical replay; no message write for conflicting replay.

FAILURE_PATH.TRIGGER: A notification was issued before recipient membership was removed, then the old event or token is activated.
FAILURE_PATH.PATH: Do not initiate new publications after current membership recheck. An already in-flight opaque event cannot be recalled. Token resolution checks current membership and fails closed; history remains restricted to allowed visibility intervals.
FAILURE_PATH.ACCESS_CHECKS: Require valid DPoP and current membership and visibility on each token resolution and history request.
FAILURE_PATH.SIDE_EFFECTS: No protected data is returned and no token mapping is consumed.
FAILURE_PATH.END_STATE: Old notification may exist, but this failed resolution request cannot disclose conversation identity or content; the token mapping remains reusable for separately authorized requests.

FAILURE_PATH.TRIGGER: Token is malformed, unknown or has no durable mapping.
FAILURE_PATH.PATH: Fail closed through protected API and return a non-disclosing failure. Do not reveal whether a conversation exists or whether the token was once valid.
FAILURE_PATH.ACCESS_CHECKS: Validate session-bound DPoP and current authorization before returning any resolution result.
FAILURE_PATH.SIDE_EFFECTS: No navigation, history retrieval, token mutation or protected data disclosure.

FAILURE_PATH.TRIGGER: Client is offline or misses one or more push events.
FAILURE_PATH.PATH: Reconnect and use cursor-based authenticated history; apply current membership visibility intervals and continue from the last valid cursor.
FAILURE_PATH.ACCESS_CHECKS: Revalidate session-bound DPoP, membership and current visibility on every history request; document ID/title metadata follows the same per-message visibility and membership-interval filters as the message.
FAILURE_PATH.SIDE_EFFECTS: Push delivery state is not treated as authoritative message state.

FAILURE_PATH.TRIGGER: A subscription contains a non-HTTPS endpoint, unexpected origin, arbitrary host, redirect or invalid scheme.
FAILURE_PATH.PATH: Reject before persisting or using the endpoint; only the configured ntfy origin is allowed.
FAILURE_PATH.ACCESS_CHECKS: Registration requires valid DPoP; register/replace additionally validate the Endpoint and subscription ownership rules.
FAILURE_PATH.SIDE_EFFECTS: No outbound request to the untrusted endpoint and no persistence of the rejected endpoint.

FAILURE_PATH.TRIGGER: Push arrives but BFE Drive session/DPoP proof is invalid or current Chat membership has changed.
FAILURE_PATH.PATH: Notification may be displayed generically, but activation cannot resolve the token or fetch history until a valid session and current authorization exist. If authorization is denied, do not disclose conversation identity.
FAILURE_PATH.ACCESS_CHECKS: Revalidate DPoP, membership and visibility; never reuse an earlier authorization decision.
FAILURE_PATH.SIDE_EFFECTS: No protected navigation or history fetch on failed authorization.

RISKS.RISK: Runtime interoperability of ntfy Server v2.34.0, ntfy Android v1.25.2 and UnifiedPush connector 3.3.5 is not proven by documentation. This gate is mandatory and remains NOT_VERIFIED until an independent runtime check is recorded.

Approved Technology grants the regular distributor identity read-only access to the broad up* pattern. The architecture preserves this approved decision and does not silently substitute per-topic ACL provisioning. Its behavior and accepted scope must be included in independent verification; changing it requires upstream Technology review.

PostgreSQL commit and ntfy publication cannot be one atomic transaction. The durable per-subscription outbox keeps committed intents durable and permits recovery of QUEUED and expired ATTEMPTED rows without a permit, while keeping network I/O outside transactions and the request response independent of delivery. DISPATCHING is not recoverable by lease expiry; without trusted confirmation that the exact worker process terminated, a row may remain DISPATCHING indefinitely. The first implementation uses one attempt per intent, terminal FAILED or UNKNOWN outcomes and no automatic retries; missed notifications are recovered through authorized history.

The mapping cannot be removed by arbitrary age-based TTL while an issued notification may still be processed. Any cleanup rule must preserve this invariant and cannot be selected in this architecture graph without an approved basis.

A push already in flight cannot be recalled after membership removal. Prevent new publications to removed memberships, and rely on mandatory current authorization during token resolution and history retrieval to prevent disclosure.
The target initializes a fresh schema and does not migrate legacy data or support old clients. Destruction, deployment and cutover decisions are outside Developer authority.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Message commits successfully; the durable delivery intent is queued; the background ntfy request times out with an ambiguous acceptance result.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: DP36-TX-MESSAGE commits message and outbox intent, the HTTP response returns without waiting for network delivery, then the worker claims and attempts the request, then records UNKNOWN through DP36-ERR-PUSH-FAILURE.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: Message remains persisted; no rollback; UNKNOWN is recorded without secrets; no automatic retry occurs; authorized history can recover the message.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: Message and outbox intent commit atomically; response does not wait for HTTP; no duplicate logical message or delivery attempt; UNKNOWN is terminal; history still enforces current authorization.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Repeat a committed message request with the same key, first with identical content and then with different content.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Identical content follows DP36-ST-IDEM-REPLAY; changed content follows DP36-ST-IDEM-CONFLICT.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: Identical replay returns original result without a new logical notification; changed content returns 409 Conflict with no new write.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Recipient activates an old opaque event after membership removal.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Notification activation to identity validation to current availability and membership checks to denied token resolution.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: No conversation identity or message content is revealed; token is not consumed; history access is denied or interval-filtered.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Client submits a malformed or unmapped wakeToken with a valid session.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Protected token resolution validates DPoP and Chat state, then fails closed on missing mapping.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: NOT_FOUND/404; no navigation, history request, token mutation or protected data.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Register, replace, or remove an account-owned push subscription while the Chat service process is available; then repeat with invalid DPoP, invalid Endpoint input, or unavailable storage.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Validate DPoP; validate the Endpoint for register/replace; scope the record to authenticated AccountID; persist only after validation. No Chat enabled/disabled gate is consulted. Invalid authentication or Endpoint is rejected; storage failure does not leave partial state.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: Subscription operations are not gated by a separate Chat state; invalid requests fail closed, valid operations affect only the authenticated account, and dependency failures follow the public error mapping.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Client misses notifications while offline and reconnects after membership visibility changed.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Authenticated cursor history rechecks current membership and filters messages by applicable visibility intervals.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: Visible messages are recovered in stable order; messages from a removed-membership gap remain hidden.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Client registers an endpoint on an origin other than configured ntfy, or supplies a malformed path, a query other than up=1, or a redirect response.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Startup validates -ntfy-origin; registration authentication and availability checks precede exact Endpoint format and origin validation; redirect responses are terminal and never followed.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: No arbitrary or malformed Endpoint is stored or contacted; no Endpoint capability is logged.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: A valid opaque event arrives, but session is expired or DPoP proof is missing/misbound when notification is activated.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Activation invokes protected API; identity validation fails before token resolution or history retrieval.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: No protected navigation, conversation identity or message content is returned.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Membership removal races with pending notification publication.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Message/recipient eligibility has defined database ordering; worker rechecks current membership before initiating publication; an in-flight event remains opaque and token resolution rechecks current membership.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: No new publication is initiated after the worker observes removal; an in-flight event cannot grant access and fails resolution after removal.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: A message includes document ID and title in its optional context; a current member and a caller outside the message's membership-visibility interval request history.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Persist only document ID/title metadata with the message; history validates current authorization and filters each message by membership visibility intervals before returning metadata.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: The authorized viewer receives document ID/title with the visible message; the unauthorized or out-of-interval viewer receives neither that message nor its document metadata. No document content is copied and Chat grants no BFE Drive rights; BFE Drive independently checks document access.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: Verify metadata appears in authorized history when present in message context; verify metadata is absent for unauthorized/out-of-interval messages; verify no document content is stored or returned and no Drive authorization is inferred.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.refs: REQ32-DOCUMENT REQ32-REALTIME REQ36-NOTIFICATION INV36-OPAQUE-WAKE AC32-REALTIME AC36-NOTIFICATION
MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: A message with optional document ID/title metadata is persisted and a realtime wake event is published to an eligible recipient.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Persist the message and metadata; create and publish only the protocol-version plus opaque-wakeToken payload; retrieve document metadata only through a separately authorized history request after token resolution.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: The realtime payload contains exactly protocol version and opaque wakeToken. It contains no message text, conversation/account identifiers, document IDs/titles or document content; metadata is available only through authorized history.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: Verify exact payload field allowlist and reject/ignore additional fields; verify history authorization and visibility filtering independently; verify wakeToken possession alone does not authorize history.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Worker stops after claim commit but before dispatch authorization.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: The row remains ATTEMPTED until lease expiry; recovery atomically changes it to UNKNOWN only if no dispatch permit was committed.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: No HTTP request, requeue or automatic retry.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: Authorization and recovery serialize on the row; no permit means no HTTP.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Worker process pauses during the five-second HTTP request after receiving a permit.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: If it resumes, it may finish its one authorized request and record the result. If the process terminates without a result, recover to UNKNOWN only after trusted confirmation from an existing process-lifecycle source. Without confirmation, leave DISPATCHING unchanged indefinitely.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: No second HTTP attempt; delivery may or may not have occurred.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: Only matching permit and WorkerID may record outcome; lease-only recovery cannot change DISPATCHING.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: ntfy responds, but the worker process terminates before committing the result.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: If termination is confirmed, recovery atomically marks UNKNOWN. If confirmation is unavailable, the row remains DISPATCHING indefinitely.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: No second attempt; ntfy may have accepted the notification.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: Outcome requires the matching permit; no lease-based recovery or automatic retry.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Lease renewal races with lease-expiry recovery before dispatch authorization.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Renewal and recovery serialize on ATTEMPTED using database time. Once authorization commits DISPATCHING, lease renewal and lease-expiry recovery no longer apply.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: Either the lease is renewed or the attempt becomes UNKNOWN; a granted permit is never revoked by lease expiry.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: Atomic row conditions distinguish ATTEMPTED from DISPATCHING.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Two recovery workers inspect the same expired ATTEMPTED row.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Only one conditional update can change the row to UNKNOWN; DISPATCHING rows are excluded from lease-based recovery.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: No duplicate transition, requeue, or retry.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: Recovery is atomic and requires ATTEMPTED status plus an expired lease.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Dispatch authorization races with lease-expiry recovery.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Both operations conditionally update the same row. If recovery commits first, state becomes UNKNOWN and authorization fails; if authorization commits first, state becomes DISPATCHING and lease recovery fails.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: There is no state in which recovery marks a permit-owning attempt UNKNOWN based only on lease expiry.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: Single-row atomic transitions; permit ID exists if and only if authorization committed.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Worker process obtains a permit, pauses until after lease_expires_at, then resumes.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: The committed permit remains valid; the same worker process may make its one HTTP request and record the outcome even though the original lease has expired.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: No second permit or request; lease expiry does not revoke authorization already granted.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: DISPATCHING is excluded from lease recovery; result checks permit and WorkerID, not the expired lease.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Worker process terminates after permit commit but before HTTP.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: The row stays DISPATCHING until an existing trusted process-lifecycle source confirms the exact worker process terminated, then atomically transitions to UNKNOWN. Without confirmation, the row remains DISPATCHING indefinitely.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: No request is issued after confirmed process termination and no automatic retry occurs.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: Lease expiry alone cannot recover DISPATCHING; termination confirmation is required.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Worker process terminates after ntfy response but before result commit.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: The current architecture has no trusted source of process-termination evidence and no recovery operation for DISPATCHING. Leave the row in DISPATCHING indefinitely, even if termination is suspected; do not infer whether ntfy accepted the request.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: Delivery remains uncertain and is never retried.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: UNKNOWN semantics explicitly allow that delivery may have occurred.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Two callers concurrently request dispatch authorization for the same attempt.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Only one atomic ATTEMPTED-to-DISPATCHING transition can create the permit; the other caller receives no permit and must not publish.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: At most one permit and one authorized HTTP attempt exist for the durable intent.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: Unique permit identity and conditional state transition prevent duplicate authorization.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: A worker process is paused or unreachable after permit grant; the current architecture defines no trusted source of process-termination evidence.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_PATH: Do not infer termination from lease expiry, elapsed time, missing heartbeat, database connectivity or service restart. Leave DISPATCHING unchanged; do not revoke the permit, mark UNKNOWN or retry.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED_RESULT: The row may remain DISPATCHING indefinitely, preserving the no-duplicate-send safety rule.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.CHECKS: No recovery operation for DISPATCHING exists in the current contract; any future recovery requires a separately approved architecture revision defining trusted evidence.
